title: If your phone is lost or stolen

cards.text: The FCC says to try your phone's find-my-phone feature. Even if it may only be lost, lock it from afar to be safe. Some apps can also wipe the data or sound an alarm.
cards.line: First, see if you can find it.

cards.text: The FCC says to tell your phone company right away. It may be able to turn off service and block the device.
cards.line: A quick call can stop more use.

cards.text: If the device was stolen, the FCC says to report the theft to the police. Some phone companies ask for proof. Change important passwords if you cannot lock the device.
cards.line: Protect the accounts that matter most.

options: Call the store where you bought it
Wait and see if it turns up
checks.why: The FCC says to try to locate the device and lock it when possible.

checks.prompt: Who should you tell about the missing phone?
options: A company that sells phone cases
checks.why: The FCC says to report the loss to your phone company right away.

checks.prompt: What should you change if you cannot lock the phone?
options: The color of your phone case
checks.why: The FCC says to change passwords for email, money, and social accounts used on the device.

takeaway: Find the phone, tell your phone company, and protect important accounts.

sources.name: FCC, What To Do If Your Wireless Device Is Stolen

situations.text: You cannot find your phone, so you use its find-my-phone feature to locate and lock it.
situations.why: The FCC says to try to locate the device and lock it from afar.

situations.text: Your phone is missing. Is it fine to wait before you tell your phone company?
situations.why: The FCC says to tell your phone company right away. It may be able to turn off service and block the device.

situations.text: If your phone was stolen, it is a good idea to report it to the police.
situations.why: The FCC says to report a theft to the police.
